Only the "on Thursday" announcement detail is lost (common to all outputs).

limitations: All six outputs are near-identical, professional rewrites with zero hard failures on the registered inventory; every figure, quote, name, direction, and attribution survives in all of them. All six also drop the source's "on Thursday" announcement timing, so C1 is uniformly altered and cannot differentiate. Ranking therefore rests on marginal meaning-preservation differences outside the inventory: A/F/C retain the source's investor-confidence framing (C drops "following the announcement"), D retains it but re-scopes the momentum framing onto international sales, and B/E omit the investor-confidence assertion (B is otherwise the most source-literal). Tier-level ordering (A/F/C > D > B/E) is fairly robust; within-tier ordering, especially A vs. F, is close.
